title: cad-bench: AIは建築2D図面をどこまで書けるか
description:
A benchmark measuring how far large language models can author 2D architectural drawings in DXF, scored mechanically.

Unlike drawing-comprehension benchmarks, the model must emit a file, and the scoring goes beyond geometric agreement to the semantics of dimensioning: whether the displayed dimension value actually matches the measured length. This is a real failure mode — Autodesk documents that DIMLFAC and text overrides cause displayed values to diverge from true lengths, and no automatic detection exists. Existing evaluation work on AI-generated CAD reports Chamfer distance, IoU, F1 and invalidity rate; none of these can see a dimension label that lies.

The task specification is derived from a prefectural design-review checklist, in which the required checks (drawing-to-drawing consistency, cross-checking against calculations and quantities) map directly onto the fields of the task spec — and in which the words for CAD, automatic, software and displayed value appear zero times.

DXF 形式の建築2D図面を書かせて機械採点する。幾何の一致だけでなく、寸法表示値と実長の整合という意味論まで問う。既存の AI 生成 CAD の評価指標では見えない失敗の型を対象にしている。

Note on data: The prefectural design-review checklist that informed the task specification is not bundled, because third-party redistribution permission could not be confirmed. The benchmark code does not reference it.

Part of the AI Practical Reach Index, a series applying one common yardstick across Japanese professional domains.
